label: Data center / IT service provider
description: A managed service provider (MSP / MSSP), a colocation or hosting provider, or an enterprise data center and IT operations group: RMM, PSA and remote-access tools that reach every customer, identity and delegated admin, hypervisor clusters, storage and backup / DR; and the critical facility behind them (utility service and switchgear, generators and fuel, UPS and batteries, chillers and CRAHs, BMS / DCIM, clean-agent suppression and EPO, PACS and mantraps). Tenants and customers in every sector bring their own notice clocks.

vocabulary.facility: the data center and managed platform (data halls, cages and racks, the power and cooling plant, the RMM / PSA, hypervisor clusters and backups)
vocabulary.public: tenants, managed customers and their users
vocabulary.frontline: NOC and SOC analysts, platform engineers, critical-facilities engineers, remote-hands technicians, security officers, service-desk agents
vocabulary.operationsCenter: the NOC / SOC and the major-incident bridge

it: RMM (ConnectWise Automate, N-able N-central, NinjaOne, Datto RMM, Kaseya VSA)
PSA / ITSM ticketing (ConnectWise PSA, Autotask, ServiceNow, Jira Service Management)
remote and privileged access (ScreenConnect, TeamViewer, BeyondTrust, CyberArk), jump hosts and VPN
identity: Active Directory, Entra ID / Okta, MFA, GDAP delegated admin into customer Microsoft 365 tenants
virtualization: VMware vCenter / ESXi, Hyper-V, Nutanix, Proxmox
SAN / NAS and object storage with snapshots and replication
backup / DR / DRaaS (Veeam, Commvault, Rubrik, Cohesity, Datto BCDR) and immutable copies
core and edge routers, firewalls, DNS / DHCP, BGP to transit carriers and DDoS scrubbing
monitoring, the public status page and on-call paging
billing, CRM, customer portal, documentation vault and password vault
ot: utility service, medium-voltage switchgear and ATS / STS
standby diesel generators with day tanks, bulk fuel and fuel polishing
UPS systems and battery strings with battery monitoring
PDUs, RPPs, busway and rack PDUs
chillers, cooling towers, CRAC / CRAH units, in-row cooling and liquid-cooling CDUs
VESDA smoke detection, pre-action sprinklers, clean-agent suppression and EPO
leak detection and temperature / humidity sensors
PACS, mantraps, CCTV, perimeter and loading dock

roles.name: Major Incident Manager (Incident Commander)
roles.description: Runs the bridge, sets severity, assigns workstreams and the update cadence, and decides when to escalate to the executive crisis team.

roles.name: Physical Security Manager / GSOC Lead
roles.description: Owns badge access, CCTV, guards, mantraps, visitor and remote-hands escort, and insider and intrusion response.

roles.name: Chief Information Security Officer (Technical Lead)
roles.description: Owns the security incident: containment (disconnect the RMM, disable federation, isolate a cluster), the IR retainer, law enforcement and evidence.

roles.name: Platform / Virtualization Lead
roles.description: Owns hypervisors, storage, backup and identity; answers 'can we restore, and how long?'

roles.name: Data Center Operations Manager / Facilities Manager
roles.description: Owns power, cooling, fire suppression, EPO and BMS / EPMS; decides load shedding, generator transfer and controlled shutdown of a data hall.

roles.name: Communications Director (PIO)
roles.description: Owns the status page, press, social media and analyst inquiries.

roles.name: Director of Customer Success / Service Delivery Manager
roles.description: Owns tenant notification, SLA credit exposure and the list of affected customers.

roles.name: General Counsel / Privacy Officer
roles.description: Owns breach-law analysis, contract notice clauses, SEC / DFARS / FedRAMP / HIPAA business-associate clocks, privilege and the cyber-insurance notice.

outsideParties: CISA and the FBI field office (IC3); the U.S. Secret Service where payment data is involved
tenants' regulators: SEC, HHS OCR, FTC and state attorneys general
DoD Cyber Crime Center (DIBNet) for defense-contractor tenants
the FedRAMP PMO and agency customers' SOCs
the fire department, local emergency management and the state environmental agency (fuel spill)
the electric utility's key-account desk and the water utility
tenants and managed customers, especially the most regulated
the RMM / PSA, hypervisor, EDR and backup vendors
UPS, generator and chiller service engineers and the fuel supplier
carriers, transit providers, the IXP and the cloud provider
the IR retainer firm, breach counsel, the cyber insurer and the ransomware negotiator
IT-ISAC, MS-ISAC, FS-ISAC and Health-ISAC (tenants' sectors)
the SOC 2 / ISO auditor and the landlord or property manager
mediaChannels: the provider's public status page and its subscriber feed
infosec researchers posting IOCs on X, Mastodon and Bluesky
customer LinkedIn posts and a downstream business's Facebook post
local TV for a generator fire or fuel spill

sceneAnchors.public: a small business front counter on a weekday morning: a cashier and a customer looking at a point-of-sale screen showing an error, a line of customers waiting, a printed sign taped to the register, bright store lighting
sceneAnchors.control: inside a network operations center: engineers at a row of desks with headsets and laptops, a wall of dark monitors, coffee cups and notebooks, dim cool light
sceneAnchors.exterior: a windowless data center building behind a tall steel fence with bollards: a row of generator enclosures and a fuel tank on a concrete pad, rooftop cooling units, a security guard booth at the gate, overcast daylight

noiseExamples: a customer asking for a password reset at 7 a.m.
a cross-connect order stuck in provisioning
a backup job warning for a single customer server
a remote-hands request to reseat a cable
a vendor renewal quote landing in the shared inbox
pressureExamples: an r/msp thread naming the provider within the hour
the largest customer's CFO threatening to invoke the termination clause
a reporter asking whether customer data was stolen
the status page subscriber count climbing while the page still says Operational
a federal agency customer asking for its one-hour incident report
a downstream business posting that its registers are down because its IT company was hacked
